newsitem.title: CHINA: China's PLA soldiers hoist red flag over garrison.
newsitem.headline: China's PLA soldiers hoist red flag over garrison.

text.p: The red flag of China flew over the former British military garrison in Hong Kong on Tuesday morning after the People's Liberation Army (PLA) planted China's stamp of sovereignty on the territory.
Chinese soldiers stood guard at the gates of the Prince of Wales Barracks, the former British military headquarters on the central Hong Kong waterfront.
The Chinese flag was flying from the garrison within seconds of the British colony being returned to China at a handover ceremony presided over by President Jiang Zemin and Britain's Prince Charles.
All the British forces had left the barracks and China's soldiers were in firm control.
Some could be seen wandering around balconies of buildings in the garrison compound surveying their new realm.
A brief colour guard was performed there at midnight on Monday (1600 GMT) in the entrance to the barracks, with six men each from the army, navy and air force of both countries.
National anthems were played while the Union Jack was lowered and three PLA soldiers hoisted the Chinese flag.
More than 100 officers and men of PLA ground, naval and air forces lined up in formation and stood in salute to the fluttering five-star red flag.

"The sacred moment which the Chinese nation yearned for for so long has arrived, and we hoist the red flag over Hong Kong now," said Major-General Xiong Ziren, political commissar of the PLA Hong Kong Garrison, in a brief address.
The British in dress uniforms marched out in formation at midnight and boarded a patrol boat.
China sent 509 PLA troops into Hong Kong three hours before the handover to join an advance guard of 196 soldiers already here to prepare for the takeover of garrison facilities.
The bulk of the new Chinese garrison forces will be pouring into the territory at 6 a.m. (2200 GMT Monday), six hours after the flag change.

That force, comprising 4,000 more troops, will arrive by land, air and sea in a huge convoy of more than 400 vehicles including a score of armoured personnel vehicles, which has been strongly criticised by Britain as sending a negative signal to the people of Hong Kong.
The garrison is also bringing in 10 naval patrol vessels and a squadron of helicopters.
China has said it may eventually match British garrison strength at its modern-day peak, roughly 10,000 personnel.
But it has not said when further contingents, if any, will come into Hong Kong after July 1.
A sizeable chunk of the garrison may remain stationed over the border in China's Guangdong province, China has indicated.
Under the 1984 treaty with Britain, China will take charge of Hong Kong's defence and foreign policy, while all other government is in local hands, with a high degree of autonomy.
Chinese officials promised the PLA would not meddle in internal security, the domain of the Hong Kong Police.
